nodes.name: Galvanic Replacement Self-Assembly Cl
nodes.procedure: Immersing clean iron foam (IF) in NiCl₂ solution at room temperature (RT) without energy input. Fe foam is redox-etched by Ni²⁺ through single displacement reaction (Ni²⁺ + Fe → Fe²⁺ + Ni), then Fe²⁺ oxidized to Fe³⁺ with assistance of water and oxygen (4Fe²⁺ + 2H₂O + O₂ → 4Fe³⁺ + 4OH⁻), finally Ni-Fe LDH nanosheets formed through coprecipitation (Fe³⁺ + Ni²⁺ + OH⁻ → Ni-Fe LDH). After several hours, color changes from silvery white to brown.

unit_operations.name: Redox Etching
unit_operations.procedure_snippet: Fe foam is redox-etched by Ni²⁺ through single displacement reaction (Ni²⁺ + Fe → Fe²⁺ + Ni)

unit_operations.name: Oxidation
unit_operations.procedure_snippet: Fe²⁺ is gradually oxidized to Fe³⁺ and OH⁻ through oxygen reduction reaction (4Fe²⁺ + 2H₂O + O₂ → 4Fe³⁺ + 4OH⁻)

unit_operations.name: Coprecipitation
unit_operations.procedure_snippet: Ni-Fe LDH nanosheets formed on Fe foam through coprecipitation of Fe³⁺ and Ni²⁺ (Fe³⁺ + Ni²⁺ + OH⁻ → Ni-Fe LDH)

nodes.characterization_summary: ICP analysis shows Fe:Ni molar ratios of 3.5:6.5 (Ni-Fe LDH/IF(NO₃⁻)), 4.6:5.4 (Ni-Fe LDH/IF(SO₄²⁻)), 5.2:4.8 (Ni-Fe LDH/IF(Cl⁻)).
nodes.evidence_snippet: Correspondingly, inductively coupled plasma (ICP) analysis corroborated that the Fe-Ni molar ratio was 3.5:6.5, 4.6:5.4, 5.2:4.8 (Table 1).

nodes.characterization_summary: SEM images show iron foam fully covered by densely packed Ni-Fe LDH nanosheets with diameter ~500 nm and thickness ~20 nm.
nodes.evidence_snippet: The SEM images (Figure 2a,b) showed that the iron foam was fully covered by the densely packed Ni-Fe LDH nanosheets. The diameter and thickness of this nanosheet is about 500 and 20 nm implying a multilayer structure.

nodes.characterization_summary: TEM images confirm clear nanosheet structure of Ni-Fe LDH/IF (NO₃⁻).
nodes.evidence_snippet: Then, it was further confirmed by TEM images (Figure 2c,d) exhibiting a clear nanosheet structure.

nodes.characterization_summary: XRD confirms successful formation of Ni-Fe LDH on Fe foam; (003) reflection peak shifts from 11.9° to 11.1° with anions Cl⁻ → SO₄²⁻ → NO₃⁻, indicating different interlayer anions and changed lattice distance.
nodes.evidence_snippet: The structural information on as-prepared materials was further examined by X-ray diffraction (XRD), which clearly implicates successful formation of Ni-Fe LDH on Fe foam (Figure 3a). ... the (003) reflection peak slightly shifts from 11.9° to 11.1° with the anions changing from Cl⁻ to SO₄²⁻ and NO₃⁻ implying that different anions were embedded into the interlayer of LDH...

nodes.characterization_summary: XPS confirms presence of Fe and Ni; Ni 2p peaks at 855.4 eV (2p₃/₂) and 873.0 eV (2p₁/₂) for Ni²⁺; Fe 2p peaks at 711.5 eV (2p₃/₂) and 724.8 eV (2p₁/₂) for Fe³⁺ in Ni-Fe LDH/IF (NO₃⁻).
nodes.evidence_snippet: As shown in Figure 3b-d, XPS results confirmed the existence of Fe and Ni elements in this NiFe LDH. Binding energy peaks at 855.4 and 873.0 eV were ascribed to Ni²⁺ 2p₃/₂ and Ni²⁺ 2p₁/₂, respectively (Figure 3c). The peaks located at 711.5 and 724.8 eV should be assigned to Fe 2p₃/₂ and Fe 2p₁/₂, respectively, indicating the existence of Fe³⁺ (Figure 3d).
